stem:
Jasper, a 2-year-old boy with asthma, has had a week of upper respiratory tract infection symptoms followed by worsening cough and wheeze. He now has persistent fever, tachycardia, tachypnoea, lethargy, poor air entry and stony dullness at the right base after 2 days of intravenous benzylpenicillin. He requires 10 L oxygen by non-rebreather mask to maintain saturations of 95%.

Which one of the following is the best course of action?

options.text: Increase the oxygen flow until the oxygen saturations are >95%
Increase the penicillin dosage and frequency to 60mg/kg/day
Increase the paracetamol dosage and frequency to maximum
Repeat the chest x-ray to exclude effusions
Continue current treatment as pneumonia requires 7 days therapy

explanation: The clinical deterioration, persistent fever, and stony dullness at the right base suggest a parapneumonic pleural effusion or empyema rather than simply slow-to-resolve pneumonia. A repeat chest x-ray is appropriate to assess for an effusion and guide further management.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: Persistent fever and signs of pleural fluid indicate complication of pneumonia requiring reassessment, not just continuation of the same therapy.

optionExplanations.A: Oxygen should be titrated to target saturations, but increasing flow alone does not address the worsening underlying cause.
optionExplanations.B: Escalating antibiotics may be needed later, but the immediate best step is to reassess for a complication such as effusion.
optionExplanations.C: Antipyretics may improve comfort but will not address the clinical deterioration.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Stony dullness and persistent sepsis suggest pleural effusion/empyema, so imaging should be repeated.
optionExplanations.E: This child is not improving as expected and may have a complication; continuing unchanged treatment is not appropriate.

source.questionTextHtml:
Jasper's clinical scenario continued

Jasper has been managed with intravenous benzylpenicillin for the last two days. He remains febrile to 39ºC, tachycardic, tachypnoeic and lethargic. He has poor air entry and stony dullness to percussion in his right base. He now needs 10L oxygen by non-rebreather mask to maintain saturations of 95%.

Which one of the following is the best course of action?

Increase the oxygen flow until the oxygen saturations are >95%

Clinical scenario 4 - Jasper

Jasper, a two year old boy with asthma, presents to the emergency department with a one week history of upper respiratory tract infection symptoms, followed by increasing coughing and wheezing over the past two days. His mother has been giving him regular salbutamol.

His vital signs are: RR 40/min, HR 150/min, Temp 39ºC and SaO

2

90% in room air.

Bronchial breath sounds are present in the right lower zone, with reduced air entry and occasional crackles. There is mild dullness to percussion over the right lower zone.

The following five questions refer to Jasper's clinical scenario.
